purpose: Bounded Fair Work Ombudsman aged-care underpayment record connecting a worker's overtime question to employer self-audit, reported back-pay, payroll correction, and an unresolved locate-and-receipt boundary.

events.geography: New South Wales and Australian Capital Territory, Australia; Southern Cross Care aged-care, home-care, and retirement-living operations
events.date_precision: official Fair Work Ombudsman media-release date; underpayment period July 2017 to October 2024 and self-audit began in 2023
events.denominator: Employer-reported 5,500 affected staff; 3,603 employees reportedly back-paid; individual case-level receipt and the full affected-worker universe are not independently audited here
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman media release and associated enforceable undertaking
events.missingness: Individual worker identity, exact underpayment, notice and claim effort, payment instrument, receipt confirmation, adequacy, household effect, later employment, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Workers were reportedly underpaid overtime, weekend penalties, shift loadings, annual-leave loading, and other enterprise-agreement allowances because of time-and-attendance and payroll-process problems
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record identifies an employee's overtime question as the trigger for self-audit but does not report individual bargaining alternatives, substitute work, household buffers, or non-use
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Underpayment transferred wage and liquidity risk to aged-care workers over a period extending from 2017 to 2024; the initiating worker's question created an institutional route to review
events.choice_or_response: An employee asked about overtime; the employer initiated a self-audit, self-reported non-compliance to the Ombudsman, and entered an enforceable undertaking; the Ombudsman required rectification and compliance controls
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled payroll, time systems, records, and payment; workers controlled whether to raise questions; the Fair Work Ombudsman controlled enforcement and undertaking oversight
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Southern Cross Care reported back-paying 3,603 employees $10,135,122 including interest and superannuation, and the undertaking requires continued efforts to locate and pay affected employees, payroll-system improvement, and compliance measures
events.remedy_receipt: The official release reports back-pay to 3,603 employees and states that wages for workers who cannot be found after 60 days will be paid into the Commonwealth Consolidated Revenue Fund; individual receipt and the remaining-worker count are not verified here
events.durability_followup: The undertaking creates payroll, training, audit, and reporting controls, but recurrence, worker-level correction, later pay accuracy, and durable household recovery are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: A worker question produced employer investigation, public enforcement, reported monetary correction, and a formal compliance route
events.protected_outcome: Some affected workers reportedly received back-pay with interest and superannuation, while the firm accepted obligations to improve payroll and compliance systems
events.sacrificed_outcome: Workers bore delayed or missing wage income and the burden of identifying or pursuing errors; unlocated workers may not receive funds directly even when the institution records a recovery route
events.cost_risk_transfer: Payroll and compliance failure shifted wage risk to workers; the undertaking shifted formal correction, locate, audit, training, and reporting obligations back to the employer
events.later_outcome: The public record reaches reported payment for 3,603 workers and a locate-and-remit rule, but not individual adequacy, household security, trust, recurrence, or exit
events.meaning_and_attribution: The institutional record attributes the problem to payroll and enterprise-agreement application failures; no worker-level trust, dignity, or meaning measure is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: A worker question and employer self-report initiated the route; no later worker collective action, political response, or worker-voice outcome is reported
events.counterexample: A worker can trigger a large institutional correction while aggregate back-pay and system-repair reporting still leave individual reachability, adequacy, and durable recovery unresolved
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release dated 2026-04-02 and associated enforceable undertaking; reported payment totals and locate rule are institutional claims, not independently audited worker receipts

arrows.evidence: The official release says an employee's question about overtime led to a 2023 self-audit and that the employer self-reported non-compliance in November 2023
arrows.counterexample: A worker question does not show that other affected workers can safely identify or raise the same issue
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker identity, effort, fear, representation, delay, and reason the question was possible

arrows.evidence: The official release attributes underpayments to time-and-attendance and manual payroll processes and reports affected overtime, penalties, loadings, and allowances
arrows.counterexample: The public aggregate release does not independently verify each worker's amount or the full affected-worker denominator
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker-level pay calculation, records, notice, and counterfactual earnings

arrows.evidence: The release reports $10,135,122 including interest and superannuation paid to 3,603 employees and a broader undertaking exceeding $11.7 million with compliance obligations
arrows.counterexample: Firm-reported aggregate correction is not the same as verified receipt for each affected worker
arrows.remaining_gap: Remaining-worker count, individual transfer timing, payment completeness, adequacy, and system implementation

arrows.evidence: The undertaking requires reasonable steps to locate affected employees, while the release states that amounts for workers not found within 60 days go to the Commonwealth Consolidated Revenue Fund
arrows.counterexample: Funds transferred to a public account may represent institutional disposition without usable worker receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-worker locate outcome, notice, claim route, receipt, and later use

arrows.to: durable pay accuracy, household security, trust, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public follow-up describes correction and future compliance measures but provides no worker-level recurrence, household, trust, or employment follow-up
arrows.counterexample: A corrected payroll process and reported payment can coexist with residual loss, unresolved trust, or later exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Later pay records, recurrence audit, household outcome, worker trust, continued work, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes a bounded worker-triggered institutional-response and reported back-pay segment. It does not establish complete worker reachability, adequacy, durable payroll compliance, household recovery, prevalence, or a general enforcement success rate.
storage_boundary: No worker, payroll, bank, or restricted data is retained; only official aggregate claims, the locate rule, and explicitly open downstream arrows are represented.
